input: Apply to speak at a local TEDx event

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether the user has a specific TEDx event in mind or needs to find one first determines whether the plan starts with research or jumps straight to applying.
Understanding who the talk is for — the intended audience — shapes the topic framing, tone, and which TEDx event is the best fit.
The user's level of prior public speaking experience affects how much preparation and confidence-building needs to be built into the plan.
A deadline or target event date dictates how urgent each step is and how much time can be spent on polishing the application.
The talk topic or idea is the core of the application — without knowing it, no meaningful guidance on crafting the pitch can be given.
Knowing what the user considers a successful outcome — getting shortlisted, delivering the talk, building a speaking career — determines how ambitious and detailed the plan should be.
Understanding what the user already has (a bio, a draft pitch, video samples) versus what is missing identifies the true starting point of the task.

gold.taskTitle: Apply to speak at a local TEDx event
gold.taskDescription: Submit a speaker application to a nearby TEDx event, covering everything from identifying the right event to crafting and sending the application.

questions.title: Do you have a specific TEDx event in mind already?
questions.description: Determine whether the user has already identified a target TEDx event or needs to research and shortlist local events first.

questions.title: What topic or idea do you want to speak about?
questions.description: Identify the core talk idea, since the entire application — title, pitch, and bio angle — is built around it.

questions.title: Who is your intended audience for this talk?
questions.description: Clarify the target listener — general public, professionals, young people, etc. — to guide how the idea is framed in the application.

questions.title: How much public speaking experience do you have?
questions.description: Assess the user's speaking background to determine whether coaching, rehearsal steps, or confidence-building activities should be included in the plan.

questions.title: Is there a submission deadline you are working toward?
questions.description: Pin down any time constraint — a specific event's application window or a personal target date — so the plan can be sequenced with appropriate urgency.

questions.title: What does success look like beyond just submitting?
questions.description: Understand the user's deeper goal — getting accepted, actually delivering the talk, growing a speaking profile — to calibrate how thorough the plan needs to be.

questions.title: What application materials do you already have ready?
questions.description: Find out what the user has already prepared — a speaker bio, pitch draft, headshot, or past talk video — to identify the true starting point and gaps.
